ports.note: A table in, a table of estimates out: one row per reported term with its ratio, interval limits and p. The design port is optional. A declared design decides the measure: a rate ratio under cohort and ecological designs, an odds ratio wherever the two-by-two allows one (a prevalence odds ratio under a cross-sectional design); anything else stops the step, saying why.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no mapping to an external vocabulary -- not meaning the terms are undeclared. fw:RegressionModel is declared in ontology/runtime.ttl, and each coefficient is an fw:EpiEstimate, the class the two-by-two uses. The receipt states the family, the outcome, the exposure and every adjustment with how it entered the model, strata, an offset, the error method, rows used and left out, strata used and dropped, and for each estimate its name, term, interval method and level. fw:RegressionModelShape and fw:EpiEstimateShape in ontology/shapes/quality-and-design.ttl hold the receipt to that. Experiment 176.

changes.description: The standard Inspector and dialog (experiment 186): the panel holds the step's Name, its input, one sentence saying the model it will fit, Configure…, and the run's own sentence on what it estimated and which rows it used and left out. Every setting moved to Configure…, on a draft that changes the step only on Apply; nothing about the model changed. With several exposure columns the run says which model it is fitting, k of n, and lets the page draw it between models; the seven models of Brazil's lag workflow held the page for 35 s with nothing moving (the practitioner, 2026-11-12).

evidence.note: Kernel unit tests: a two-by-two as logistic regression gives its odds ratio and Woolf's standard error; an unadjusted Poisson model gives the rate ratio; absorbed strata give the coefficients of the model with stratum indicators. Published figures reproduced on the authors' own data: NYC ozone 1.0609 per 10 ppb, coefficient and HAC standard error equal to the authors' archived R result to 12 significant figures; Salmonella Galia melon adjusted for age group (7 groups) and sex, 96 (15-2067) and 18 (4.6-101) against the published 96 (15-2100) and 18 (4.6-100). Nothing here establishes that a model is well specified. One model per exposure column (0.4.0): each model's estimates equal the single model fitted on that column alone, and each uses exactly the rows its own column has a value on, never the rows common to all (tests/regression-per-exposure.test.mjs, synthetic data). Not yet compared with Validation Lab checks 36 and 37 or the 2010-2025 figures in experiment 182. 0.6.0: tests/regression-per-exposure.browser.mjs and tests/salmonella-from-scratch.browser.mjs set the model in Configure… and check the Inspector's sentence; Chromium. tests/regression-per-exposure.test.mjs: fitted one at a time, the models equal those fitted together, each announced before it is fitted.
